title: Depth in a queried-coordinate tree
statement: Let $C$ be a list of coordinates, $s\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ a seed, and $F:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathcal{T}$ a map into coordinate decision trees. If the tree formed by querying the coordinates in $C$, branching over both bit values and updating the seed accordingly, has depth at least $k$, and $|C|<k$, then some $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ satisfies $\operatorname{depth}(F(x))\ge k-|C|$.
hypotheses_covered: C is a list of coordinates
F maps Boolean-cube inputs to coordinate decision trees
The constructed query tree has depth at least k
The length of C is strictly less than k
